interpretation: At exactly 1 Hz, the 292.092Hz pair magnitude is 0.0669734% of the full yaw transfer and 0.4595918% of the full roll transfer. Its arithmetic subtraction hardly moves the unmatched drawing ratios: yaw 1.2756673 to 1.2764940, roll 0.6706973 to 0.6703193.

For 800-to-1600 endpoint grids, removing the saved 292 Hz pair difference reduces the roll discrepancy maximum from 3.5762695% to 1.8172942%, with the remainder maximum at 0.02875s. At the original full maximum 0.1375s, the normalized remaining roll difference is 1.2051082%.

For 1600-to-3200, the roll remainder after subtracting 292 Hz is 2.2177474% versus original 2.2086588%. For 3200-to-6400 it is 5.6793323% versus original 5.6797866%, both maxima 0.0090625s. The selected 292 Hz pair therefore accounts for a substantial part of the earlier grid difference but essentially none of the latest one.

The single 292 Hz projection passes the original 1e-6 gate on every saved grid, with maximum relative identity difference 4.52744e-8. Five pairs pass; the weak 284.894 Hz pair fails at 2.45005e-6 to 2.64589e-6. The six-pair sums and remainders remain qualified diagnostics, not an all-six validated reconstruction.

This is a retained-array decomposition. It proposes no physical removal, filter, mode truncation, revised integration scheme or accepted temporal accuracy. It does not resolve the original Bode operating-point mismatch.
